title: From quanta to qubits
dek: A century and a quarter separates Planck's quanta from the first error-corrected logical qubits. Physics supplied the paradoxes, mathematics the language, and computer science the question: what could be computed with all this? Filter by chapter to follow each thread.

eras.title: The quantum revolution
eras.text: Energy comes in packets, particles behave like waves, and in barely a decade the theory acquires its definitive mathematical form: vectors in Hilbert spaces.

eras.title: Paradoxes and information
eras.text: Entanglement goes from an embarrassing paradox to a testable inequality, while information theory discovers that computing has a physical cost.

eras.title: The idea of a quantum computer
eras.text: Feynman proposes simulating nature with quantum machines, Deutsch defines the universal quantum computer and the first problems with a quantum advantage appear.

eras.title: Algorithms and codes
eras.text: Six extraordinary years: Shor's and Grover's algorithms, the first error-correcting codes, the threshold theorem and the first qubits in the laboratory.

eras.title: Building qubits
eras.text: Nuclear magnetic resonance, trapped ions, superconducting circuits, photons: a slow engineering race towards more qubits with fewer errors.

eras.label: 2018 – today
eras.title: From NISQ to fault tolerance
eras.text: Noisy processors with dozens to hundreds of qubits, the first claims of quantum advantage and, finally, error correction below the threshold.

events.title: Planck's quanta
events.text: To explain the radiation of hot bodies, Planck assumes that energy is exchanged in discrete packets.

events.title: The photon
events.text: Light itself comes in quanta: the explanation of the photoelectric effect, which earned Einstein the Nobel Prize.

events.title: The Stern–Gerlach experiment
events.text: Silver atoms in a magnetic field split into exactly two beams: the first measurement of a qubit.

events.title: Matrix mechanics
events.who: Werner Heisenberg, Max Born, Pascual Jordan
events.text: Observable quantities are represented by matrices that do not commute.

events.title: Schrödinger's equation and Born's rule
events.text: The wave function evolves linearly; its squared modulus gives probabilities.

events.title: The uncertainty principle
events.text: Position and momentum cannot both have sharp values. Robertson proves the general version in 1929.

events.title: Electrons that interfere
events.text: Electrons scattered by a crystal produce an interference pattern: matter behaves like a wave.

events.title: Hilbert spaces
events.text: Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik gives the theory its rigorous form: states are vectors, observables are operators.

events.title: EPR and entanglement
events.who: Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, Nathan Rosen; Erwin Schrödinger
events.text: Einstein argues that quantum mechanics is incomplete; Schrödinger names the phenomenon Verschränkung, entanglement.

events.title: Boolean circuits
events.text: A master's thesis shows that relay circuits obey Boole's algebra: the birth of digital logic.

events.title: Bras and kets
events.text: The notation $\ket{\psi}$ that every textbook still uses.

events.title: The Bloch sphere
events.text: To describe nuclear magnetic resonance, Bloch represents the state of a spin as a vector on a sphere.

events.title: The sum over paths
events.text: The amplitude of a process is the sum of the amplitudes of all the paths that lead to it.

events.title: Landauer's principle
events.text: Erasing a bit dissipates at least $k_BT\ln 2$ of heat: information is physical.

events.title: Bell's theorem
events.text: No local hidden-variable theory can reproduce all the predictions of quantum mechanics.

events.title: The CHSH inequality
events.who: John Clauser, Michael Horne, Abner Shimony, Richard Holt
events.text: A version of Bell's inequality that can be tested in the laboratory with photons.

events.title: Reversible computation
events.text: Every computation can be done without erasing information, and therefore without Landauer's cost.

events.title: The Holevo bound
events.text: $n$ qubits cannot transmit more than $n$ classical bits of information.

events.title: RSA
events.who: Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir, Leonard Adleman
events.text: Public-key cryptography based on the difficulty of factoring.

events.title: Toffoli gate and quantum Turing machines
events.text: A universal reversible gate, and the first model of a computer obeying quantum mechanics.

events.title: The Tsirelson bound
events.text: Quantum correlations can reach, but not exceed, $2\sqrt2$ in the CHSH game.

events.title: “Simulating physics with computers”
events.text: In a lecture at MIT (published in 1982), Feynman argues that simulating quantum systems requires computers that are themselves quantum.

events.title: Aspect's experiments
events.who: Alain Aspect, Jean Dalibard, Gérard Roger
events.text: Entangled photons violate Bell's inequality with polarizers switched during the flight.

events.title: The no-cloning theorem
events.who: William Wootters, Wojciech Zurek; Dennis Dieks
events.text: An unknown quantum state cannot be copied.

events.title: BB84
events.text: The first quantum key distribution protocol: an eavesdropper cannot copy qubits without disturbing them.

events.title: The universal quantum computer
events.text: Deutsch defines a quantum Turing machine able to simulate any physical process, and gives the first problem with a quantum advantage.

events.title: One electron at a time
events.text: The double-slit experiment with single electrons: the interference pattern builds up dot by dot.

events.title: The Deutsch–Jozsa algorithm
events.text: One query decides with certainty whether a function is constant or balanced.

events.title: BQP and the Bernstein–Vazirani problem
events.text: The foundations of quantum complexity theory: the class BQP and the first superpolynomial oracle separations.

events.title: Quantum teleportation
events.text: A Bell pair and two classical bits transfer an unknown qubit.

events.title: Simon's algorithm
events.text: An exponential separation against randomized classical algorithms, for a periodicity problem. It inspires Shor.

events.title: Shor's algorithm
events.text: Factoring and discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a quantum computer. The field explodes.

events.title: The first quantum code
events.text: Nine physical qubits protect one logical qubit against any single-qubit error.

events.title: Ion-trap gates
events.who: Ignacio Cirac, Peter Zoller; Christopher Monroe, David Wineland
events.text: A proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and, that same year, the first experimental two-qubit gate.

events.title: Phase estimation
events.text: A general framework for quantum algorithms that estimate eigenvalues.

events.title: Grover's algorithm
events.text: Unstructured search with $O(\sqrt N)$ queries instead of $O(N)$.

events.title: The Steane code
events.text: A seven-qubit code built from a classical Hamming code.

events.title: Search cannot be faster
events.who: Charles Bennett, Ethan Bernstein, Gilles Brassard, Umesh Vazirani
events.text: Any quantum search algorithm needs $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ queries: Grover's is optimal.

events.title: The threshold theorem
events.who: Dorit Aharonov, Michael Ben-Or; Alexei Kitaev; Emanuel Knill, Raymond Laflamme, Wojciech Zurek
events.text: Below a constant error rate, arbitrarily long quantum computations are possible.

events.title: The Gottesman–Knill theorem
events.text: Clifford circuits, however entangled, can be simulated efficiently by a classical computer.

events.title: A superconducting qubit
events.who: Yasunobu Nakamura, Yuri Pashkin, Jaw-Shen Tsai
events.text: Coherent control of a qubit made from a superconducting electrical circuit, the technology of today's largest processors.

events.title: DiVincenzo's criteria
events.text: Five requirements for building a quantum computer, from scalable qubits to long coherence times.

events.who: Lieven Vandersypen, Isaac Chuang and colleagues (IBM)
events.text: Shor's algorithm factors 15 with seven nuclear spins in a molecule.

events.title: “Quantum supremacy”
events.text: Preskill coins the term for the point at which a quantum computer does something no classical one can do in a reasonable time.

events.title: Bell without loopholes
events.who: Groups in Delft, Vienna and Boulder
events.text: Three experiments close the main loopholes of Bell tests at the same time.

events.title: Quantum computing in the cloud
events.text: A five-qubit processor becomes available to anyone over the internet.

events.title: The NISQ era
events.text: Noisy intermediate-scale quantum: useful processors before error correction?

events.title: Sycamore
events.text: 53 superconducting qubits sample random circuits in 200 seconds, a task estimated to be extremely costly for classical supercomputers (an estimate later reduced by better classical algorithms).

events.title: Jiuzhang
events.who: Jian-Wei Pan, Chao-Yang Lu and colleagues (USTC)
events.text: A photonic quantum advantage experiment based on the interference of dozens of photons (boson sampling).

events.title: Nobel Prize for entanglement
events.who: Alain Aspect, John Clauser, Anton Zeilinger
events.text: For experiments with entangled photons that established the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneered quantum information science.

events.title: Dozens of logical qubits
events.who: Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail Lukin and colleagues
events.text: A neutral-atom processor runs algorithms on up to 48 error-detected logical qubits.

events.title: Post-quantum standards
events.text: FIPS 203, 204 and 205: the first standards for cryptography designed to resist quantum computers.

events.title: Below threshold
events.text: On the Willow processor, the logical error of a surface code halves each time its distance increases: the threshold theorem, seen in the laboratory.

events.title: RSA-2048 with under a million qubits
events.text: A new resource estimate lowers the cost of breaking RSA-2048 to less than a million noisy qubits running for under a week.

events.title: Nobel Prize for superconducting circuits
events.who: John Clarke, Michel Devoret, John Martinis
events.text: For the discovery of macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantization in an electric circuit, the physics behind superconducting qubits.
